rationale: Two earlier limitations recorded that the pendingReadIndexMessages path was never exercised, so this turn probes it explicitly and also records its mechanism as sourced knowledge. stepLeader's MsgReadIndex branch appends the request to r.pendingReadIndexMessages and returns without broadcasting when the leader has not committed an entry in its current term (raft.go:1346-1363); releasePendingReadIndexMessages is invoked only from the MsgAppResp path when maybeCommit first advances the commit (raft.go:1542-1546) and feeds each queued message into sendMsgReadIndexResponse (raft.go:2123-2157). The harness reaches that state by making a real node campaign and win without any follower acknowledgment, so the new entry is not committed yet, then submits a local ReadIndex, observes the queue, delivers the replication messages so the followers acknowledge the entry, and records that the queued request is released and answered.

investigations.question: Does a ReadIndex request that reaches a leader before it has committed an entry in its current term get delivered once that first commit happens, or can it remain queued while the leader keeps making progress?
investigations.hypothesis: A MsgReadIndex submitted before the leader's first commit in its term is appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages with no heartbeat broadcast, and the queue is drained only in the MsgAppResp-driven commit path, which the leader's own first commit in the term triggers; the queued request is then served by the usual ReadOnlySafe path.
investigations.discriminator: Make a node win an election without any follower acknowledging its entry, submit a local ReadIndex while committedEntryInCurrentTerm is false, and record the queue size, the emitted heartbeats and the delivered read states; then deliver the replicated entry to the followers, step their acknowledgments back, and record whether the queued request is released and delivered with the new commit index. The same probe also submits a ReadIndex after that commit as the contrast path. If the queued request stays queued after the commit, or if it was answered before the commit, the hypothesis is refuted.
limitations: The probe submits the read request from the leader itself, so the delivered read state is the leader's own; a forwarded request from a follower would additionally exercise the MsgReadIndexResp path.

The leader is put into its pre-commit state by calling becomeCandidate/becomeLeader directly instead of waiting for an election round trip, because the intermediate state is otherwise not observable; the state itself is the library's normal post-election state.
Only the default ReadOnlySafe and a three-voter cluster are covered.

knowledge.statement: In stepLeader, a MsgReadIndex whose sender passes the leader checks is answered immediately through sendMsgReadIndexResponse only when the leader has committed an entry in its current term; otherwise the message is appended to r.pendingReadIndexMessages and no heartbeat is broadcast, so the request is held without any progress signal. releasePendingReadIndexMessages, invoked from the MsgAppResp handler when maybeCommit first advances the commit index, then feeds every queued message through sendMsgReadIndexResponse, which under the default ReadOnlySafe registers the request, records the leader's own acknowledgment and broadcasts a heartbeat carrying the rctx.
knowledge.conditions: StateLeader with the default ReadOnlySafe; the read request reaches the leader before its first commit in the current term; the leader stays leader and the commit that releases the queue is driven through the MsgAppResp path.

scope.description: One probe on a freshly built three-voter cluster whose node 1 is made leader without any follower acknowledgment, so it has no committed entry in its term. The probe submits a local ReadIndex, observes the queue, then delivers the replication messages and the followers' acknowledgments to drive the first commit, and finally submits a second ReadIndex after that commit as the contrast path.
assumptions: The leader is made to win directly (becomeCandidate + becomeLeader) so that the pre-commit state is observable; this is the same state the library reaches momentarily after a real election.
Read requests are submitted locally by the leader, which steps a MsgReadIndex exactly as Node.ReadIndex does.
All messages are delivered in process with no loss, and the followers are ordinary fresh raft instances configured with the same voter set.
The default ReadOnlySafe option is used, so an answer requires the leader's own acknowledgment plus a quorum of voter acknowledgments produced by the real followers.
excluded: ReadOnlyLeaseBased and forwarded read requests from followers
Snapshots, restarts, membership changes, leadership changes and network faults
Any application-level interpretation of the delivered read state

experiment.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). The test builds three real raft instances with newTestRaft(1|2|3, 10, 1, newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))), calls r1.becomeCandidate() and r1.becomeLeader() so that node 1 leads with an uncommitted entry in its term, and takes r1.bcastAppend()'s messages while recording committedEntryInCurrentTerm() (expected false). It then steps a local MsgReadIndex carrying the rctx into the leader and emits read_index_queued with committed_in_term, committed, queued_after, heartbeats_emitted, read_states_after and the leader state, which shows whether the request was queued with no heartbeat broadcast. Next it delivers the leader's MsgApp to nodes 2 and 3 through a bounded queue, steps the MsgAppResp acknowledgments they produce back into the leader, and emits read_index_released with the new committed index, committed_in_term, queued_after, read_states_after, delivered, read_state_index, undelivered_messages and leader state. Finally it submits a second local MsgReadIndex, delivers the two heartbeats it produces to the real followers, steps their acknowledgments back, and emits read_index_immediate with queued_after, read_states_added, heartbeats, acks_from_voters, delivered, committed and leader state. The test asserts the precondition (no committed entry in term before the queued request) and that both requests are delivered, so a change in either path fails the harness instead of reshaping the evidence.
experiment.responsibility: The leader-side ReadIndex producer owns eventually answering a read request that it accepted for later processing: a request that the leader deferred because it had no committed entry in its term must be released by the commit that makes the read index available, not left waiting for an unrelated later proposal.

comparisons.description: A ReadIndex request deferred before the leader's first commit in its term is delivered once that commit happens.
